canonicalRecords.title: portable data versus host-local state

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given credentials and local machine paths exist in operational storage, when a project is cloned, then none appears in its versioned tables or history.
Given A performs an offline TODO edit and creates audit E1, when connectivity returns without a Dolt commit, then hub audit contains exactly E1, A retains E1, and main/remote remain C0.
Given E1 was stored but its receipt was lost, when the same batch retries, then exactly one E1 exists and the same hash receipt returns; changed payload under E1 returns409 audit_id_conflict.
Given source has100 TODO audit and20 generic audit rows, when seed/join audit backfill verifies, then all120 records have matching payload hashes and hub receipts; missing one blocks cutover.

Given an explicitly promoted sanitized session with turns, actions, dialog, commits/files, PlanFile and TodoId, when cloned, then every promoted child and relationship matches the source snapshot; automatic capture still uses the audit channel.
Given accepted head changes C0 to A1, when the derived index rebuild completes, then queries read A1 values and no C0 cache is served under the A1 key.
Given main=C0 is clean, when heartbeat, audit and automatic session capture run, then Dolt working-set fingerprint remains unchanged.
Given agent1 owns the editing lease, when agent2 logs a session action, then its local audit persists without acquiring or changing agent1's lease.
Given a promoted snapshot contains a fixture secret detected by the configured detector, when commit preview runs, then422 secret_detected creates no commit and outputs no secret value.

Given unique fixture canaries are injected through protected secret references, when commands, retries and failures execute on both hosts, then scans of argv, receipts, logs, chat/audit payloads, memory stores, generated files, Git staged blobs/new commits and Dolt working sets/new history find zero canary values. Scanner diagnostics and rejected commit previews also contain zero values; no secret is added to history to test the detector.

canonicalRecords.body: Separate versioned project content from operational state while delivering permanent audit to the hub independently of commits and excluding secrets.

canonicalRecords.title: scoped authorization and offline behavior

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given A has a valid Atlas token, when A addresses the private backend across the link, then the connection fails; when a read-only token attempts a public-main mutation, then403 unauthorized_project; when a publish-authorized token bypasses publication.accept through a raw public-ref push, then409 publication_required. In all three cases remote/main remains C0.
Given token has Atlas.read but no SecretProject scope, when a remote fetch requests SecretProject, then403 unauthorized_project sends zero objects.
Given A holds a reference token, when IdentityServer disables A and revokes its grants before acceptance, then accept returns401 invalid_token and remote/main is unchanged.
Given hub/IdentityServer is unreachable and a valid authorized local user, when a local TODO edit is requested, then it succeeds; an unauthorized local user still receives403.
Given ordinary editing SQL credentials, when remote administrative procedures or public-ref writes are attempted, then permission is denied and no object publication occurs.
Given IdentityServer revocation completes, when A starts new fetch and publish requests with its old token, then both return401 invalid_token before transfer or ref mutation.
Given both services run, when LAB probes10.42.0.143:3306 and LEGION probes10.42.0.214:3306, then both connections fail; local127.0.0.1:3306 health succeeds.
Given the peer uses an unapproved SPKI or wrong SAN, when control/remote TLS connects, then tls_peer_untrusted occurs before bearer transmission.

Given a plugin session has Atlas.read but lacks publish, when capabilities load and a publication is nevertheless attempted, then publish is unavailable in the capability display, the request returns403 unauthorized_project, the denial is explicit and no SQL/CLI fallback or head change occurs.

canonicalRecords.body:
Reuse integrated IdentityServer for single-user node ownership, per-node client credentials, project scopes and revocation; preserve authorized offline work.

Server: least-privilege capabilities plus server-side authorization on every call. Plugin: show available rights and explicit denial; capability display never substitutes for authorization.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given desired=7 and reported=6, when poll runs twice, then both responses request7 and stored reported remains6.

canonicalRecords.body: SyncSubscription key=(NodeId,ProjectId,Branch) contains HubEpoch UUID, PublishedHead, PublishedGeneration int64, DesiredGeneration int64, ReportedGeneration int64, WorkerEpoch int64, AcceptedHead, Outcome and timestamps. POST control/poll is read-only. POST control/report includes all epochs and observed generation; stale worker=409 stale_worker_epoch, stale hub=409 hub_epoch_changed. Poll every30s with20% jitter; commit/reconnect/on-demand wake immediately. Backoff1s doubling to60s. Generation ordering is valid only within HubEpoch. Restore generates a new non-reused random epoch before listeners reopen.

canonicalRecords.body: Project history excludes secrets and automatic operational audit. This does NOT make audit local-only: every host retains permanent local audit and an append-only outbox delivers sanitized records to the hub unversioned ledger independently of project commits. AuditRecord key=(OriginNodeId,RecordId UUID); fields ProjectId,EntityKind,EntityId,OriginSequence int64,OccurredUtc,Actor,Action,PayloadVersion,PayloadHash,Payload. POST audit/batches validates token/project, inserts atomically by key and returns per-record durable receipts. Same key/hash is already_received; same key/different hash=409 audit_id_conflict. No UPDATE/DELETE permission. Local pruning is forbidden. Migration backfills TODO and generic audit history with counts/hashes and receipts. Credential values are excluded at capture, not silently replicated.

canonicalRecords.body:
Reuse existing Duende IdentityServer. Provision client fed.node.{NodeId} per single-user node, bound to ownerSubjectId through authenticated operator enrollment. Client credentials issue short-lived reference access tokens; audience qbrain-federation and scopes fed.project.{ProjectId}.{read|publish|control|audit|enroll}; protected actions additionally require server membership/branch permission. Gateway introspects without positive caching for each new request and rechecks before publication commit; unavailable identity returns503 identity_unavailable. Revoke through IdentityServer: disable client and remove its persisted reference grants. Gateway rejects inactive tokens401 invalid_token; do not invent a revocation ledger. Native remotesapi uses gateway-held credentials over loopback; clients cannot access it directly. Ph0 proves token injection/relay including redirects/object URLs, project isolation and no public-ref bypass.

Server: least-privilege capabilities plus server-side authorization on every call. Plugin: show available rights and explicit denial; capability display never substitutes for authorization.

Ph0 B5 binds the exact restored Duende 7.4 patch and matching source-tag/API references, and proves issuance, introspection, grant removal and revocation against that binary. General/v8 documentation alone cannot close B5.
